content: CD120, also known as Cluster of Differentiation 120, refers to two distinct members of the tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR) superfamily. These are tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1) and tumor necrosis factor receptor 2 (TNFR2). Receptor Subtypes There are two variants of the CD120 receptor, each encoded by a separate gene: 1. CD120a (TNFR1) Also referred to as TNFR superfamily member 1A. TNFR1 is the receptor subtype responsible for mediating the effects of TNF-alpha, particularly in inducing sickness behavior. It plays a significant role in neurotoxic processes. 2. CD120b (TNFR2) Also referred to as TNFR superfamily member 1B. Elevated levels of TNFR1 have been observed in individuals with severe mental disorders, suggesting its involvement in the pathophysiology of these conditions.
